pattern: A focusable canvas (group, roledescription 'canvas') containing two multi-select listboxes, one for nodes and one for connections, each with one roving tab stop (WAI-ARIA APG listbox, with spatial arrow navigation for nodes). Each node's accessible name states its label, shape, and connections; a text alternative table lists every node with what it leads to and comes from. Edits have keyboard and single-pointer paths (no deprecated ARIA drag-and-drop attributes) and are announced through live regions.

roles.role: button (native); Pan tool, Connect, and Move selection are toggles (aria-pressed)
group with aria-roledescription 'canvas', named by label; focusable (arrow keys pan)
option with aria-roledescription 'node', named '{label}, {shape}, leads to …, comes from …'
listbox (aria-multiselectable), named '{label}: connections'; hidden when there are none

roles.element: connector drawing, groups, grid, overlay, label text

roles.role: button (aria-expanded, aria-controls) and a region with a table (caption, column and row headers)

aria.value: label; '{label}: nodes'; '{label}: connections'; computed node and connection names; '{label} controls'; 'Label of {name}'
true for selected nodes and connections
0 on the focused node and the focused connection, -1 on the others
true at the zoom limits and when undo, redo, delete, Move selection, or Connect is not possible
Whether the table is shown / the table region id

Polite: zoom, added, deleted, moved, connected, reconnected, label changed, copied, pasted, undone, redone, layout applied, cancellations. Assertive: move mode, connecting from, Move selection prompt, refused connection, locked node.

keyboard.action: Toolbar buttons, palette (edit mode), canvas, the focused node, the focused connection, then the text alternative.
Pan the view (Shift: four times farther).
Move focus to the nearest node in that direction (spatial, not mirrored in RTL); Shift adds it to the selection.
First / last node in reading order.
Select only this item / toggle it in the selection.

keyboard.context: Node or connection focused, edit mode
keyboard.action: Edit the label inline (Enter or leaving the field commits, Escape cancels).
First press: this node is the source ('Connecting from …'); move to the target and press C or Enter to connect. C on the source again cancels.
Move mode for the node (or the selection): arrows move by one grid step (Shift: five), Enter or M finishes (one undo step), Escape restores.

keyboard.context: Node or connection focused, edit mode
keyboard.action: Delete the selection (or the focused item); deleting nodes deletes their connections. Locked nodes stay.
Copy / cut the selected nodes (with the connections between them) / paste them offset.
Zoom in / out around the center; fit to screen.
Cancels connecting or Move selection, else clears the selection.

focus: One node and one connection are in the Tab order (roving tabindex): the last focused, else the first in reading order. Focusing a node pans the view so it is fully visible. Re-rendering keeps focus on the same element; after deleting, focus moves to the first remaining node (or the canvas); after adding from the palette or pasting, focus moves to the new node; the label editor returns focus to its item. Nodes show a focus-ring rectangle; connections a ring along their path.
notes: Every dragging action has an alternative (2.5.7): moving by M plus arrows or by the toolbar Move selection button then a single click on the canvas; connecting by C on source and target or the Connect button then a click on the target; adding shapes by clicking palette buttons; panning with arrow keys on the canvas; reconnecting by deleting and connecting again.
Node names include their connections, and the text alternative table lists the whole graph, so the structure is available without seeing the drawing (1.1.1, 1.3.1).
Selected nodes differ by fill and a three px outline, connectors by width, not color alone (1.4.1).
Ports are small pointer targets (2.5.8); the keyboard and toolbar connect paths are the equivalent controls.
knownCaveats: Manual screen-reader verification (NVDA, JAWS, VoiceOver) is pending.
Screen readers in browse mode may intercept arrow keys and letters; users need focus mode inside the diagram.
Pointer drags (move, connect, marquee, pan) are not announced while they happen; the result is.
Spatial arrow navigation can skip nodes hidden behind others in the same direction; Home/End and the text alternative reach every node.
